answer: Making every identity solve a fresh proof-of-work puzzle raises the summit an attacker must climb before a single fake can earn. Each marble of compute spent on one account cannot be reused for the next, so spawning ten thousand Sybils means paying ten thousand times the electricity and time, while one honest agent pays once. The horizon of cheap mass forgery closes: the cost scales linearly with the attack, and puzzle difficulty can rise automatically whenever new identities flood in.
